diagnosis: Repeated operations are overrepresented in candidate/bad runs: 1,485 versus 224 operations, a raw 6.63× difference and +1,261 signed excess. They constitute 20.16% of bad operations versus 5.93% of good operations (3.40× normalized) and occur in 88 bad versus 20 good source sessions.
expected_mechanism: Detecting unchanged action-state-result cycles and requiring a changed strategy should prevent unproductive retry loops, improving progress per operation. The cost is small bookkeeping and deliberation overhead, plus occasional premature abandonment of retries that might eventually succeed.
policy_text: Before repeating an action on the same target, compare the latest state and result with the previous attempt. If neither changed, do not retry unchanged: alter the strategy, target, parameters, or information source. After two equivalent failures, explicitly reassess the subtask and choose a different approach or stop.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -s '{bad_total:([.[]|select(.value>0)|.value]|add),good_total:([.[]|select(.value<0)|-.value]|add),bad_repeated:([.[]|select(.value>0 and .stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated")|.value]|add),good_repeated:([.[]|select(.value<0 and .stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated")|-.value]|add),bad_sessions:([.[]|select(.value>0 and .stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated")|.labels.source_session[0]]|unique|length),good_sessions:([.[]|select(.value<0 and .stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated")|.labels.source_session[0]]|unique|length)}' samples.jsonl
quantitative_evidence.finding: bad_total=7,366; good_total=3,780; bad_repeated=1,485; good_repeated=224; bad_sessions=88; good_sessions=20. Thus repeated shares are 20.16% and 5.93%, respectively.
The signed candidate-minus-base excess for repeated operations is +1,261.
